required_floor_classes.lane_definition: A veterans scenario cannot pass if eligible veterans, survivors, caregivers, or dependents lose earned eligibility, health access, claims access, housing access, or service availability below reviewed floors.
A veterans scenario cannot pass if lower cost is achieved by degrading care quality, claims accuracy, timeliness, disability determination quality, safety, or appeal rights.

A veterans scenario cannot pass if burdens shift to disabled veterans, rural veterans, women veterans, low-income veterans, homeless veterans, survivors, caregivers, or high-need cohorts without reviewed evidence.
A veterans scenario cannot pass if service adequacy, health outcomes, housing stability, employment outcomes, crisis capacity, or claims resilience falls below reviewed floors.
A veterans scenario cannot pass without eligible cohort, service package, statutory continuity, transition cost, workforce/care network, claims system, and implementation feasibility models.

veterans_specific_floor_definitions.definition: Earned eligibility, statutory continuity, survivor/caregiver/dependent eligibility, and grandfathering rules require explicit reviewed floors.
VA and community-care access, mental health, specialty care, rural access, wait times, and continuity require sourced baseline, policy, and stress values.
Claims timeliness, backlog, accuracy, appeal rights, disability determinations, and remediation capacity require explicit thresholds.
Housing stability, homelessness prevention, employment outcomes, income transition, and high-need supports require reviewed values.
No target cost can be selected without an eligible cohort, service package, statutory continuity review, transition cost, and delivery feasibility model.

public_warning_phrases: This veterans floor packet defines required floor concepts, but it does not set threshold values or pass/fail findings.

No lower-cost veterans scenario is admissible until earned eligibility, health access, claims timeliness, housing/employment outcomes, statutory continuity, equity, adequacy/resilience, and delivery-feasibility floors are thresholded, sourced, reviewed, and passed.
No target cost can be selected without an eligible cohort, service package, statutory continuity review, transition cost, and delivery feasibility model.
No target cost, federal effect, gross savings, net savings, solver input, department-cut instruction, technology-savings claim, or balanced-budget claim is populated.
No FOIA request, records request, form, email, phone call, or agency/person contact was submitted.

This record is not outcome-floor passage, not an eligible cohort model, not a service package model, not a statutory continuity finding, not a federal score, not a target-cost selection, not solver input, not a solver run, not a rate calculation, not a public rate card, not a savings estimate, not a waste finding, not a fraud finding, not a department-cut instruction, not a technology-savings claim, and not a balanced-budget claim.
